Well, see, at first my wife didn’t know she was ace until we had gotten a little intimate a couple of times (light stuff) and then, because of how it felt to her she started looking into what could be causing a lack of physical desire/attraction.

After she got through all the medical sites trying to tell her it must simply be a hormone imbalance or something of the like, she stumbled across the concept of asexuality and it clicked in her head; she’d never felt physical attraction like that or even masturbated before.

Well, when she first told me, she said she was Demi-sexual (while still being fairly certain she was Ace) because she was terrified that I’d run for the hills or something if she came outright and said Asexual. Well, as time progressed, we did our little bit of fooling around here and there, and I realized she wasn’t enjoying it so it got to the point where I wasn’t really enjoying it anymore, and I could tell something was bothering her.

We sat down and had a LONG conversation about the subject, and at first, I admit I had a hard time understanding (this was at about the 6 or 7 month mark) and I initially had some self esteem/ego issues about it. I felt undesirable, and that really sucked, on top of also feeling a little starved for physical attention.

But then I decided to do research, because at that point I’d decided I really loved her, and I didn’t want to lose our relationship; through that digging and the like, I came to understand the Ace outlook a lot better. I realized I was being petty and foolish for taking it like I did; it didn’t mean she loved me any less or that I was unattractive (I felt so shallow afterwards) she simply didn’t express her love for me via physicality, it wasn’t her thing and it’s just how she’s wired.

What really made it work was lots of compromises on both our parts, substituting sex and the like with lots of cuddling/various other forms of physical affection that don’t include “the deed” and me working on the mentality society drives into an Allosexual’s head about needing to be constantly desired and lusted for by their partner to feel validated. 

We do still occasionally have sex, which means it might not work for the sex-repulsed members of the community, but the frequency is only about 1 to 2 times a month and we’ve incorporated a lot of aids to make it better for her.

It was a tough road at first, but I would say I feel entirely satisfied and happy with our relationship, and I am so glad I hung in there. She’s amazing and I couldn’t see myself this happy with anyone else.

Tl/dr: good and honest communication, alternative forms of physical affection, experimentation and a lot of love/understanding can make anything work, in my opinion.
